title: Independent Xitsonga dam-bank bounded reuse check
sourceEnglish: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
currentNativeTarget: Swiharhi swi nga onha tibangi ta damu na ku engetela vulongo ematini. Ku va kona ka swona a swi endli mati ma basa kumbe ma hlayiseka.
currentDeckTarget: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Ku va kona ka swona a swi endli mati ma basa kumbe ku hlayiseka.

meaningJudgment: At model semantic level, retaining only the noun “banks” preserves the source’s physical bank referent in this dam/water paragraph and avoids relying on an unverified Xitsonga loan “tibangi.” The surrounding translated clause still expresses animals can damage the banks and add manure into the water; the second sentence still says their presence does not make the water clean or safe.

bankTermFinding.reasonForNounOnlyHold: I cannot independently verify that “tibangi” reliably names a dam embankment in Xitsonga. Preserving exact “banks” avoids a possible lexical ambiguity without leaving the whole sentence in English.

limits: Meaning/source check only. No fluent Xitsonga, local farming, Shangani, or production approval. The noun “banks” is an exact English hold; only the surrounding ordinary prose is recommended for reuse.
